programmes.d: Mike and Carol plan a camping trip for the whole family.
Carol gets laryngitis right before singing at the Christmas service.
Marcia nominates Mike for a Father of the Year award.
The Bradys comb the neighborhood in search of runaway dog Tiger.
Mike and the kids run the house while Carol is out of town.
The stag party thrown by Don's buddies costs him his engagement to Ann.
Ann gets a modeling assignment at Belmont Racetrack and Don's buddies get caught up in betting.
Ann is assigned to picket in front of the Newsview Magazine building where Donald works. Donald tries to make amends by inviting his boss to Ann's house for dinner.
Stuck in an elevator, Donald and Ann reminisce about their last five years together.
Ann has just gotten an acting job for a television commercial filming in the lobby of the office building, but an encounter with the chivalrous Donald may put her new job at risk.
Ann Marie moves out of Brewster, New York to an apartment in New York City, with the help of her agent Harvey Peck and much to the chagrin of her father.
When Oscar's ulcer begins acting up, Felix decides an ocean voyage will do them both good.
To understand each other better, Felix and Oscar reverse their roles -- Felix turning to a slob and Oscar becoming a fussbudget.
Felix gets Oscar in trouble with the Internal Revenue Service.
To raise funds for his financially troubled amateur opera club, Felix induces Oscar to arrange for a gambling event.
Felix and Oscar are arrested and charged with ticket scalping.

The kids are at each others' throats. The basic cause of the problem is that the house is seemingly too small with six kids sharing two bedrooms and one bathroom.
Jan gets a locket from a secret admirer. As the family try to determine who anonymously sent the locket, they're momentarily distracted when Jan loses the locket.
Greg wants to quit school to become a major league pitcher.
Greg and Marcia baby-sit their siblings for an evening.
Ann agrees to babysit for her neighbor and friend Judy Bessemer, who assures her that she'll be back long before Ann has to leave for her audition for an acting workshop.
As Ann borrows Donald's car to move a rubber tree plant, a sewing machine salesman (Carl Ballantine) distracted by a pretty girl bumps into the car and sues her for damages.
Ann talks Don into a drive to Brewster to pick up her old hi-fi system, which leads to an on-the-road picnic that goes wrong.
While paying a parking ticket, Ann meets a rich young man (Sam Melville) who invests in the theater and tries to seduce her, much to the chagrin of Donald.
When Donald's secretary goes on maternity leave, Judy Bessemer suggests hiring Ann as a substitute.
After burning a hole in Felix's bed, Oscar despairs of raising the money for a new one. But a poker session with his old college friend, Monty Hall, leads to an idea.
When Oscar's mother fears for her son's social life, Felix finds him an-old-fashioned Greek girlfriend.
As a surprise for Oscar, Felix paints the apartment flaming peach, sells the old furniture at a rummage sale and refurnishes the apartment with futuristic pieces.
When Murray's wife ejects him from their home, Felix invites him to share his and Oscar's apartment.
Oscar is literally put out when Felix invites his former wife to share the apartment while her house is being painted.
